papers.title: Isoflurane anesthesia CNS recovery state: ultra-slow oscillations and cellular-stress-responsive gene expression
papers.summary: Compared recovery from 4 h isoflurane anesthesia with time-matched sleep and sleep deprivation in mice using EEG/EMG and frontal cortex RNA sequencing; isoflurane recovery produced transient rebound arousal, fragmented NREM, and persistent ultra-slow oscillations normalizing within two weeks, with cortical transcriptomics distinct from sleep deprivation (integrated stress response/unfolded protein response enrichment vs. growth-permissive mTOR-associated profile).

papers.title: HP-GSBS: Accelerating greedy state boundary search with reusable interval statistics
papers.summary: HP-GSBS is an open-source Python package that accelerates Greedy State Boundary Search by reusing interval contributions and correlation statistics, with streaming candidate reduction, local refinement, and shared CPU/CUDA/Triton backends. Across seven controlled workloads it achieved median same-input speedups of 154–1730× while reproducing original boundaries and state counts (max absolute t-distance difference 1.88×10⁻¹¹), with complementary validation on four frozen EEG recordings.

papers.title: Sleep Stage Classification Across Heterogeneous EEG/EOG Channels with Multi-channel Differential Transformer.
papers.summary: Proposed SleepDIFFormer, a multi-channel differential transformer framework using cross-domain alignment for domain-generalizable sleep stage classification from raw heterogeneous EEG/EOG, and reported superior performance versus existing approaches across five sleep staging datasets under domain generalization settings.

papers.title: Enhancing cortical electrophysiological signatures of sleep overrides ER stress responses in sleep-deprived mice
papers.summary: In sleep-deprived mice, flickering light stimulation during deprivation prevented upregulation of activity-dependent and unfolded protein response (ER stress) genes while further increasing NREM slow-wave activity, and induced brief neuronal OFF periods resembling sleep-like cortical states. The authors conclude that physiological manipulation of cortical activity can dissociate molecular ER-stress signatures from electrophysiological sleep-pressure markers.

papers.title: Circadian and Sleep-Wake Modulation of EEG Functional Connectivity Across Brain States and Its Associations With Cognition in Humans.
papers.summary: Using over 1,200 hours of artifact-free EEG from a 10-day forced-desynchrony protocol, the study showed that sleep-wake history and circadian phase both modulate EEG functional connectivity, with sleep-wake history having broader influence. Global connectivity increased across NREM sleep (especially delta and sigma bands) but declined during REM, and state-specific connectivity measures were associated with cognitive performance.

papers.title: Single-Lead EEG-based virtual reality motion sickness detection using interpretable feature selection.
papers.summary: Proposes a SHAP-based single-lead EEG modeling and feature-screening framework for lightweight virtual reality motion sickness detection, selecting lead FT11 and seven handcrafted features for XGBoost classification. Under window-level tenfold cross-validation it achieved 87.53% ± 0.73% accuracy, with a post hoc LOSO test showing limited cross-subject generalization.

papers.title: Comparing re-referencing methods for human intracranial EEG
papers.summary: This study compared re-referencing methods on macro-contact and microwire SEEG data from 16 epilepsy patients performing an episodic memory task, finding that method choice altered artifact-rejection survival, low-frequency power, and aperiodic background. In hippocampal recordings, however, no method changed the magnitude or direction of the memory effect in power or spike-field coherence.

papers.title: Beyond Mean Pooling: Statistical Meta-Aggregation for Subject-Level EEG Classification in Parkinson's Disease
papers.summary: The authors propose statistical meta-aggregation that summarizes each subject's epoch-wise EEG predictions with 14 distribution descriptors instead of mean pooling, using a self-supervised contrastive encoder in 90 subjects (57 Parkinson's disease, 33 controls). Replacing mean pooling raised subject-level ROC-AUC from 0.655 to 0.872 for logistic regression and from 0.724 to 0.840 for SVM without changing the encoder or classifier family.

papers.title: Artefact-free EEG during temporal interference stimulation reveals phase-specific modulation of the human visual cortex
papers.summary: Develops a front-end analogue low-pass filtering and per-recording artefact verification pipeline to record artefact-free EEG during temporal interference stimulation, then tests phase-specific neuromodulation of the visual cortex in 22 healthy participants. In-phase 15.5 Hz TI increased SSVEP amplitude at 14.5 and 15.5 Hz and shortened response times relative to sham and anti-phase TI.

papers.title: Template-Anchored Signal Decomposition and Label Refinement for Impairment Categorization on Noisy Visual Electrophysiological Data.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: Constructs a dataset of ERG and VEP recordings from 1,970 participants and proposes a template-anchored signal decomposition method with joint channel-spatial attention and soft-label refinement for three-class visual impairment categorization. The method consistently outperformed existing electrophysiology-based and general biosignal classification approaches.

papers.title: Bombadil: A Foundation Model for Plant Electrophysiology
papers.summary: Bombadil is a foundation model for plant electrophysiology pretrained without labels on over 4 million hours of electrical signals from 100 plant species across ten environments. It tracks changes in seven physiological indicators of plant stress, including in species and stressors with no labels in training.

papers.title: A feature-optimized EEG framework using multiscale entropy and metaheuristic optimization for cognitive analysis.
papers.summary: The study applied multiscale entropy features (dispersion, permutation, sample, fuzzy) with filter- and wrapper-based feature selection to EEG from 100 participants to distinguish sports from non-sports groups. Genetic Algorithm optimization yielded a minimal feature subset with 93.0 ± 2.7% nested cross-validated accuracy using SVM, and five classifiers showed mean Fleiss' kappa of 0.874 ± 0.051.

papers.title: Nonlinear Feature Modeling Using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Electroencephalography for Depression Classification: Deep Learning Study.
papers.summary: Introduces Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (ConvKAN and ConvKAN Efficient) for EEG-based depression classification on frequency-domain features using the EDRA dataset. ConvKAN Efficient achieved accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score all exceeding 94%, outperforming conventional CNN and traditional machine learning methods.

papers.title: Amplitude-integrated electroencephalogram (aEEG): A bedside window into newborn brain function in the NICU.
papers.summary: This review describes amplitude-integrated EEG (aEEG) as a bedside tool for neonatal brain monitoring in the NICU, emphasizing its role in hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy evaluation and first-line seizure detection alongside conventional video EEG. It argues that integrating aEEG into multimodal neuromonitoring improves neurodevelopmental prognostication and individualized bedside intervention.

papers.title: Combined eye tracking and electroencephalography during referential selection in dyadic interaction.
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study synchronized mobile EEG and eye tracking via LabStreamingLayer during a simplified director task to compute overlap-corrected regression-based ERPs time-locked to spoken nouns and fixations. Targets competing with occluded referents elicited a stronger posterior positivity, fixation timing modulated neural responses, and competitors received little visual attention; analysis scripts and datasets are openly available.

papers.title: Aperiodic neural activity predicts cortical excitability in TMS-EEG
papers.summary: Single-pulse TMS-EEG in healthy adults (n=29 M1, n=11 DLPFC) showed a strong negative relationship between the pre-stimulus aperiodic exponent and early local TMS-evoked potential amplitude in both regions, with steeper 1/f-like slopes associated with smaller EL-TEPs and inconsistent alpha/beta power relationships.

papers.title: A spatio-temporal attention convolutional network with topology-preserving channel embedding and transformer for EEG decoding.
papers.journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
papers.summary: The paper proposes E-STACNet, a spatio-temporal attention convolutional network with topology-preserving channel embedding, convolutional layers, and multi-head self-attention for EEG decoding. It reached average accuracies of 88.00% and 80.62% on BCI Competition IV 2a and Giga DB, and 96.49%/96.46% for valence/arousal on DEAP, outperforming state-of-the-art models.

papers.title: EEG Resting-State Beta Band Dynamic Functional Connectivity Reveals State-Dependent Disruption of Language Network Lateralisation in First-Episode Schizophrenia.
papers.summary: In first-episode schizophrenia patients, dynamic EEG beta-band functional connectivity revealed state-dependent disruption of language network lateralisation, with reduced laterality in a specific brain network state (BNS1) that correlated with language disorganisation scores.

papers.title: Cross-Modal Masked Connectome Transformer for multimodal EEG-fMRI learning in ADHD diagnosis.
papers.summary: A Cross-Modal Masked Connectome Transformer (CM-MCT) for EEG-fMRI fusion achieved 89.7% accuracy and 94.3% AUC in ADHD diagnosis, using ROI-level masked connectome modeling and cross-attention.

papers.title: Supramodal Coding of Detection and Confidence in the Human Cortex
papers.summary: Intracranial stereoelectroencephalography in eight epilepsy patients performing a near-threshold audiovisual detection task revealed a largely supramodal cortical detection code (including insula, dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, superior temporal gyrus) whose multivariate decoders generalized across modalities, and a substantially supramodal confidence architecture including cross-modal confidence coding in sensory cortices.

papers.title: An amygdala-mediated simulation-to-decision cascade aligns interbrain dynamics to solve social dilemmas.
papers.summary: Using intracranial EEG from epilepsy-patient dyads playing iterated prisoner's dilemma, the study found amygdala interbrain representational alignment during mutual cooperation, with early theta suppression and later low-frequency suppression/gamma increases supporting a simulation-to-decision cascade.

papers.title: Variable task difficulty with augmented sensory feedback for motor training in virtual reality.
papers.summary: In a VR-based upper-limb motor training study with 14 neurotypical participants, augmented sensory feedback modality and task difficulty differentially modulated behavioral, physiological, and perceptual outcomes, with visual+haptic feedback during straight-line training yielding the largest reductions in path length and completion time.

papers.title: Late Integration of Prior Expectations During Precision-Weighted Perceptual Decisions.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: Two preregistered EEG experiments (N=80) showed that prior expectations in a visual motion task are integrated late during response planning, as revealed by multivariate inverted-encoding models, rather than modulating early sensory encoding.

papers.title: Responses to unannounced rule changes in adults with developmental disabilities: A community-based pilot study with consumer-grade EEG
papers.summary: In a community-based pilot with adults with developmental disabilities, a probabilistic reversal learning task and consumer-grade resting-state EEG showed wide interindividual variation in switch bias; a flatter frontal aperiodic spectrum was associated with fewer switches after negative feedback and more perseverative errors, and frontal alpha peak amplitude correlated with accuracy. The authors present this as preliminary evidence that field EEG can capture individual differences in responses to unannounced change.

papers.title: Spectral power and functional connectivity of resting EEG in people exposed to armed conflict and controls
papers.summary: Resting-state EEG was compared between 74 Colombian adults exposed to armed conflict and 48 controls, analyzing spectral power and functional connectivity across multiple bands. No EEG contrast survived correction for multiple comparisons, indicating that large or widespread alterations were not detectable; occipital/global alpha power and temporal theta showed only nominal differences.

papers.title: Cognitively demanding motor exercise and subsequent inhibitory control: Behavioral and ERP Evidence.
papers.summary: In a within-subject study, 40 healthy young adults performed a whole-body Motor-Cognitive Integrated Task with either high or low cognitive demand (matched for physical load) before a flanker task with EEG. Higher cognitive demand was associated with reduced flanker interference and altered conflict-related N2 modulation and overall P3 amplitude, without accuracy differences.

papers.title: Selection vs. integration task demands shape the similarity of information neural coding
papers.summary: Using EEG in a cue-target size-judgment paradigm, the study examined how selection versus integration task demands shape neural coding during preparation and target processing. Decoding showed categorical templates active in both phases under selection but only during preparation under integration, and RSA indicated exemplar encoding sustained post-stimulus during selection but not integration.

papers.title: Effects of EEG neurofeedback in adults with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a systematic review of randomised and non-randomised studies.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-guided systematic review of seven studies (three RCTs, four non-randomised; n=390) synthesised clinical, cognitive, and electrophysiological outcomes of EEG neurofeedback in adult ADHD. RCTs showed small, generally non-significant effects versus controls, while naturalistic and personalised protocols reported large symptom reductions; no treatment-related adverse events were observed.

papers.title: Bridging the Gap Between Design and Access: Toward Visual Scene Displays for Brain-Computer Interface Use in Augmentative and Alternative Communication by Children.
papers.journal: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR
papers.summary: In 24 neurotypical children aged 8–13, asymmetric placement of items in photographic visual scene displays increased frontal and centro-parietal P300 amplitudes and contextual scenes enhanced the occipital N170, while offline predicted P300 BCI accuracy was similar to a standard grid and scenes were rated more visually appealing. The findings support preliminary feasibility of integrating contextual scene displays into pediatric BCI augmentative and alternative communication.

papers.title: Is Less More? Exploring the Visual Processes of Minimalist and Complex Photography Through Eye Tracking and EEG.
papers.summary: Thirty participants viewed minimalist versus complex photographs while eye tracking, consumer-grade EEG, and subjective assessments were recorded. Minimalist images elicited fewer fixations and saccades but longer single fixations, more concentrated hotspots, lower perceived complexity, greater relaxation, and higher attention eSense levels, with no aesthetic difference.

papers.title: Ketamine's mechanisms of action in major depressive disorder and treatment-resistant depression: Is brain topological change a candidate convergent systems-level pathway?
papers.summary: This narrative review integrates molecular, circuit, neuroimaging, and electrophysiological evidence to evaluate whether normalization of pathological brain network topology is a convergent systems-level pathway for ketamine's antidepressant effects. It proposes that ketamine rapidly increases global connectivity, reduces rigid network organization, and enhances neural signal diversity in association with clinical improvement.

papers.title: Neural Response to Monetary and Social Feedback in Childhood: Processing Reward and Loss in Relation to Peer Outcomes and Anxiety Symptoms.
papers.summary: In 106 children aged about 8 years, EEG event-related potentials to monetary and social feedback were examined in relation to anxiety and peer functioning. Children showed greater neural response to monetary loss than reward but greater response to social reward than loss; anxiety predicted greater monetary reward response, and in highly anxious children greater social-loss response predicted worse peer relations.

papers.title: EEG signature in psychiatrist's subjective experience: a pilot study.
papers.summary: In a pilot study with two psychiatrists and ten patients, the authors recorded clinician EEG during a clinical interview and ACSE administration and found dimension-specific, topographically distinct oscillatory patterns and connectivity differences for the Difficulty in Attunement and Engagement dimensions. These preliminary findings suggest clinicians' subjective experiences during clinical encounters may be associated with measurable neural signatures.

papers.title: The effect of text-picture consistency on memory integration in college students: Evidence from ERPs.
papers.journal: The British journal of educational psychology
papers.summary: In 28 college students, an adapted pictorial demonstration paradigm with simultaneous ERP recording showed that text-picture consistency improved memory integration (58% vs. 48%) and that inconsistency elicited a larger late P600 (500-800 ms) but no significant N400 difference, implicating late conflict/integration processing.

papers.title: Early neurocognitive outcomes following SEEG with radiofrequency thermocoagulation.
papers.summary: In a prospective study of 28 patients across two epilepsy centers, neuropsychological testing before and about 3 weeks after SEEG with radiofrequency thermocoagulation found no group-level global or domain-specific cognitive decline, with only 1/28 declining on at least two measures and most patients returning to work by about 4 weeks.

papers.title: Mapping the Research Landscape and Global Trends: A Bibliometric Analysis of Event-related Potential in Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.summary: Bibliometric analysis of Web of Science publications on event-related potentials in Alzheimer's disease, covering publication trends, collaboration networks, and keyword clustering; identified six research themes (P300/N200, MMN, N170, N400, OERP, EEG) and suggested mismatch negativity as a future hotspot.

papers.title: The translational asymmetry of corpus callosotomy: Two literatures that answered different questions.
papers.summary: This review searched three databases and identified 62 experimental animal studies (1948-2026) of corpus callosum or forebrain commissure sectioning with epilepsy-related outcomes, finding that almost none varied the extent of section or compared the three clinical extents against seizure control and cognitive outcomes. The authors argue the translational gap is methodological, requiring new animal experiments that model graded disconnection and the selective posterior operation.

papers.title: Narrow Is Slow: CT-Derived Anatomic Isthmus 3 Width and Arrhythmogenic Substrate in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot
papers.summary: In a retrospective single-center study of 27 adults with repaired tetralogy of Fallot undergoing electrophysiology study, CT-derived anatomic isthmus 3 width was significantly narrower in patients with slow-conducting isthmus 3 (18.4 ± 6.6 mm vs 29.2 ± 9.0 mm; p = 0.001), and width above 21.5 mm had an 80.0% negative predictive value. The authors propose CT isthmus measurement before pulmonary valve replacement as a non-invasive aid to invasive risk stratification.

papers.title: Twenty Years at the Crossroads: Is Clinical Cardiac Electrophysiology Science, Procedure, or Both?
papers.summary: A review/perspective reflecting on twenty years of clinical cardiac electrophysiology, examining whether the field is best characterized as science, procedure, or both, with attention to ablation, arrhythmology, atrial fibrillation, and training.

papers.title: Elucidating the relationship between protein amide I, II, and III bands and secondary structures by localized anharmonic vibrational calculations.
papers.summary: Used localized second-order vibrational quasi-degenerate perturbation theory combined with QM/MM and MD snapshot averaging to compute amide I, II, and III spectra of the insulin dimer and ubiquitin; found amide II and III peak positions closely track coil contributions, whereas the amide I maximum origin is more protein dependent, and hydrogen-bond-dependent amide I shifts correlate with O=C-N-H dihedral changes.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
